records.title: Do you assess the compliance status of devices during conditional access?
records.description: Conditional access is at the heart of Zero Trust. The decision to grant appropriate authorization must take into consideration the access context including the compliance status of the device, which will rely on the information provided by the device's EDR or MTD solution. It is therefore important to be able to integrate the EDR/MTD with the conditional access engine that will take into account the trust level of the device in its access policies. In the Microsoft environment, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint integrates with Azure AD as well as third-party MTD solutions through Intune.

records.title: Are you proactively updating the drivers and firmware of your devices?
records.description:
Updating the drivers and firmware of devices remains a real challenge for administrators, due to the need to identify the drivers for each device, the frequency of updates, the size of the packages... Most of the time, these updates are deferred and only performed when the OS version changes. However, security incidents are often mitigated by driver updates and require a quick intervention of services.
Microsoft recommends using Windows Update to manage and control driver updates, including in a hybrid mode where other updates (OS, applications, etc.) are managed by an internal tool. In a Zero Trust vision, a management of the workstations from a cloud MDM is still recommended with a complete management of the updates from Windows Update, which allows a better reactivity and a reduction of the work for the administrators.

records.title: Do users need to use a VPN when they are off-site?
records.description:
More and more applications are available as SaaS (especially collaborative services such as Microsoft 365) and are therefore accessible from the Internet. It is becoming difficult to justify the systematic use of full VPN, which requires traffic to be redirected to the internal network, for performance reasons that are all the more important for real-time traffic such as video. The use of VPN should be reserved for internal applications (e.g. legacy applications) that you do not want to make accessible from outside.
The answer in a Zero Trust vision is to ensure the security of devices through the use of an EDR/MTD, to rely on the conditional access control system and to authorize exceptions on the VPN tunnel when accessing to trusted services or applications.

records.title: Have you implemented network segmentation/micro-segmentation best practices for your cloud applications and services?
records.description:
Traditional segmentation approaches typically fail to achieve their goals because they were not developed in a way that aligns with business use cases and application workloads. This often results in excessive complexity requiring large firewall exceptions.
In a Zero Trust approach, networks are segmented into smaller "islands" where specific workloads are contained. Each segment has its own egress controls to reduce the "detonation radius" in case of unauthorized data access. Implementing software-defined perimeters with granular controls increases the difficulty for attackers to move through the network and reduces the opportunity for lateral movement. When cloud solutions implement it, direct and private connections between services are to be preferred. For example, in Azure, Private Endpoints allow a direct private connection through the Microsoft network to Azure Private Link services without the flows going out to Internet. (See also https://docs.microsoft.com/fr-fr/azure/private-link/private-endpoint-overview).

metadata.link_label: Secure networks with Zero Trust | Microsoft Docs

records.title: Do you have widespread encryption of communications in an environment where devices are mostly located outside the organization and applications are mostly hosted in the cloud?
records.description: In a perimeter vision, network flows are not encrypted internally, which allows them to be analyzed to detect threats. Once outside the organization's perimeter, all communications that pass over the Internet must be encrypted to guarantee their confidentiality. In a Zero Trust approach, the traffic between the user/device and the resource is encrypted from end to end, and the detection of threats is no longer done at the network level but at the identity, device and resource level (by privileging communication tools and applications offering end-to-end encryption).

records.title: Have you improved the security posture of your applications by moving them to the cloud?
records.description:
Migrating applications to the cloud allows you to take advantage of tools such as "Cloud Security Posture Management" (CSPM) to continuously assess the security level of your applications and "Cloud Workload Protection" (CWP) to detect threats to resources and workloads in a multi-cloud environment.
In addition, when applications are removed from the internal network, they are less likely to be compromised by typical internal attacks based on lateral movement and privilege escalation.

records.title: Is Azure AD your identity repository for all your applications including  business applications?
records.description:
Deploying a reference directory for identities is a prerequisite for the implementation of Zero Trust. It is the cornerstone that will allow to centrally control access to all applications in accordance with the conditional access policies you define. Azure AD plays this central role by providing, through strong authentication, a guarantee of the identity that connects and conditional access to applications provided they are integrated with it.
Azure AD comes with a gallery containing several thousand of pre-integrated applications, but it is also possible to integrate any application already present in your organization, or any third-party application from a vendor that is not already part of the Azure AD gallery.

Multi-factor authentication requires the user, in addition to a password, to provide an additional form of identification, for example a code on the cell phone or a fingerprint. Integrated since Windows 10, Windows Hello Enterprise replaces passwords with a strong two-factor authentication. This authentication is based on biometrics or a PIN code and is linked to the device used. The removal of passwords usage significantly reduces the attack surface and the risk of identity compromise.
See also Passwordless Strategy.

records.title: Have you provided a data labeling system?
records.description:
The classification defines different levels or categories (e.g. Public, General, Confidential, Sensitive) which will be expressed in the form of labels. 
Manual labeling: users (as data producers) have the possibility to assign labels to documents or emails associated with their sensitivity level.
Template-based labeling: Classification can be based on automatic recognition against templates. The labeling system must have a large number of predefined templates that will be able to identify sensitive information by analyzing the content and making comparisons to detect, for example, social security or credit card numbers.
AI-based labeling: Use of Machine Learning-based classifiers when content is not easily identified by manual or automated pattern matching methods. The system can provide a number of pre-trained classifiers as well as the ability to train your own classifier.

metadata.link_label: Learn about sensitivity labels - Microsoft 365 Compliance | Microsoft Docs

records.title: Do you have a process that users are aware of in the event of a data breach?
records.description:
The GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) has considerably strengthened the obligations of organizations in case of a data leak. The organization must notify the data leak to the data protection authority within 72 hours after discovery and inform the affected individuals as soon as possible.
The data leakage can be due, for example, to the compromise of an application, but it can also be the responsibility of an employee without any intention to harm. Therefore, it is necessary to have a process in place that is known to all employees to notify immediately of any leak of personal data.
Solutions can be put in place to limit the risk of data leakage (see DLP above) that will cover both services and devices, but the definition of a notification process is still necessary.

metadata.link_label: Breach Notification - Microsoft GDPR | Microsoft Docs

records.description:

For example, the notion of a "Landing Zone" defines a conceptual architecture encompassing all the services required to host workloads based on best security practices.
In addition, Azure Blueprint enables cloud architects to define a repeatable set of Azure resources that implement and adhere to an organization's standards, templates and requirements. Azure Blueprint enables development teams to quickly create and implement new environments that conform to an organization's requirements with a set of components, such as networking, to accelerate development and delivery.

records.description: DevSecOps automatically integrates security into every phase of the software development lifecycle, enabling secure software development in an Agile/DevOps mode. DevSecOps implies the respect of security best practices from the very first phases of development, thus focusing on security more than on the final audit and on the initial development using a shift-left strategy. In a Zero Trust vision, the secure development of applications is all the more critical as they are exposed on the Internet.

records.title: Have you implemented a vulnerability check of the source code of your applications, a dependency check in the code of your applications and their patch levels to prevent supply chain attacks?
records.description:
Security development practices (SDLC) require code analysis (static and dynamic), as well as a set of good practices related to the application life cycle.
In addition, supply chain attacks are more and more frequent, especially due to the reuse of vulnerable opensource components (OpenSSL, Log4j, etc). It is therefore important to apply a fine control of dependencies (libraries, service, API, code, etc.) in order to quickly identify inherited vulnerabilities.

records.title: Is a team in charge of security and Zero Trust involved in the architecture and implementation phases of your internal applications?
records.description: Consideration of security, and more specifically the principles of Zero Trust, from the architecture phases is necessary to ensure that applications will be properly protected, integrate with identity services, respect network segmentation principles, protect secrets, and take advantage of the security controls available in the platform that hosts them. For example, the notion of a "Landing Zone" defines a conceptual architecture encompassing all the services required to host workloads based on best security practices. This "landing zone" can then be deployed through an Azure landing zone accelerator.

records.title: Have you deployed a Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM) and Cloud Workload Protection Platform (CWPP) solutions to ensure the security of your applications on your various cloud and on-premise environments?
records.description:
A CSPM solution provides a continuous assessment of the security level of your applications (workloads, VMs, resources, etc.) and issues security recommendations to reinforce the security posture. The Cloud Workload Protection (CWP) feature adds threat detection on resources and workloads in multi-cloud and on-premises environments.
In addition, alerts can be sent to the SIEM/SOAR.

records.title: Have you published a policy for managing secrets in cloud and on-premises applications? Implementing vaults and secure vault access allows for the segregation of developer and application access to secrets.
records.description:
The management of sensitive enterprise secrets, keys and certificates (and associated private keys) is a critical process in the security posture and regulatory compliance. A secret management policy should be defined that is based on security best practices that dictate how these sensitive assets are managed.
For example, the use of a key vault such as Azure Key Vault can ensure the storage of secrets, but care must be taken to ensure that access is audited and that the principle of least privilege is respected.

records.title: Do you consider the target application or service in the access control?
records.description: In the conditional access control engine, access policies can be targeted more specifically to applications or services. Administrators can add any application registered with Azure AD into conditional access policies, whether it is a Microsoft cloud application (Office 365, Intune, PowerApps, Teams...), a gallery or non-gallery application, as well as applications published via the application proxy.
